item.title: One Quarter of Minority Ethnic Students Experience Racism at Least Once a Month, According to New Survey
item.description: A report revealed today that a quarter of all minority ethnic students in Irish secondary schools said they experience racism at least once a month. Most of these students claimed that they experienced it once a week or more and commonly expressed their concerns about the casual use of racial slurs by their peers and the lack of consequences for this language. item.title: The Resurgence of Diet Culture
item.description: Over the break, my family and I decided to sit down and watch a movie on cable television back in the United States. During the ad breaks, I noticed a peculiar thing: every single ad was for a weight loss drug, makeup brand, or fitness program. There were no more film trailers, cereal jingles, or even ads for visiting Texas anymore. I began to reflect and realize the world around me after this event. Young women in society are being fed constantly to lose weight and how thin is back “in” again.

item.title: Jane Freyer Elected Auditor of the Hist Amid Election Mishaps
item.description: Jane Freyer was officially elected Auditor of the 257th session of the College Historical Society (Hist) at 6:39 p.m. today. Freyer received 67 votes out of a total of 96 valid votes from Hist members. item.title: Abbey Street Closed, Red Line Luas Partially Disrupted Following Serious Collision
item.description: A collision has shut down Abbey Street and halted Red Line Luas service between Smithfield and The Point. The incident occurred around 1:25pm on April 1st at the junction between Abbey Street and O’Connell Street in Dublin. The accident was attended by ambulances, the fire brigade, and An Garda Síochána who have now left the scene. Road users are still advised to avoid the area due to delays.
